# Notes of this project for coding agents

Issue assistant: A GitHub Action that looks after issues: a first analysis by an AI that only reads, labels, duplicates and reminders, all checked before posting.

This file belongs to the project: the blueprint wrote it once, and its updates leave it alone. It adds to `AGENTS.md` what a coding agent needs to know about this project alone, such as its architecture, the commands of its own checks and what to watch for in its tests.

## Where things are

- The action is defined in `action.yml` and runs `issue_assistant.py`.
- `README.md` documents installation, configuration and use, `docs/` holds the pages of the website, and `CHANGELOG.md` lists the changes of every release.
- The tests are in `tests/`; `scripts/check.sh` runs every check.
- The weekly Mutation workflow runs the tests in mutmut's copy, `mutants/`, where `issue_assistant.py` holds every mutant beside its function. A test that reads the script as text, with `read_text()`, `open()` or `inspect.getsource()`, can't pass there and gets `@pytest.mark.mutation_unsafe`; a check of behaviour that it makes as well goes into a test of its own. `tests/test_mutation_safety.py` finds each unmarked one that reads it in its own module; it doesn't follow helpers of `conftest.py` or `support.py`, so keep such reads out of them. The help of the commands and options lives in the tables `SCRIPT_COMMANDS` and `SCRIPT_OPTIONS`, and `main()` hands each command to a function of its own: mutmut copies a whole function for each of its mutants, and leaves the constants of a module alone.
- The Action test, `.github/workflows/action-test.yml`, runs the action as its users run it. Each of its jobs ends with the step *Explain the failure*, and each step of a job belongs to a part that the PR coach explains from `.github/checks.project.toml`; a new job, step or part comes with its explanation, which `tests/test_coach.py` checks.
- The Workflow test, `.github/workflows/workflow-test.yml`, calls every reusable workflow as a dry run, and its job *reusable workflows*, a required check, reads the jobs of its run with `scripts/workflow_test.py`. A renamed job of a reusable workflow, or a renamed step that writes the plan of a dry run, goes into `CALLS` of that script in the same pull request; `tests/test_workflow_test.py` checks it. Every job of a reusable workflow starts its checkouts with the guard that stops it when GitHub names no commit of the workflow, which `tests/test_templates.py` keeps in each.
- GitHub runs only its own actions and those that `[actions.selected]` of `.github/repository.toml` lists. A new action that only the workflows of this project run, such as an action of a new engine, goes into `patterns_allowed` of `[actions.selected]` in `.github/repository.project.toml`, in the same pull request; `tests/test_repository_settings.py` checks it, and the settings bot fails on `main` without it. An action that such an action only runs in turn goes there too, and into `RUN_IN_TURN` of that test.
- The pictures in `docs/images` show what the assistant posts: `scripts/images/pages.py` builds their pages from its texts, and `bash scripts/render-images.sh` takes them, with Docker, and writes `scripts/images/manifest.json`. A change of a text of `locales/`, of the cleaning, of a page or of `scripts/images/style.css` that a picture shows fails `test_the_pictures_show_what_the_assistant_posts` until you run the script and commit the pictures and the manifest; the screenshot bot renders them anew after a new version of the tools.
